author: Declaration Desk
title: Bangladesh PM calls emergency meeting as garment wage protests shut 529 factories
dek: Tarique Rahman met ministers on Sunday evening after workers set a police vehicle on fire under a Dhaka metro station. Owners threaten temporary closures if work does not resume, while workers press for a Tk 30,000 minimum wage.

body:
Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held an emergency meeting with senior ministers on Sunday evening as protests by garment workers demanding higher pay spread across Dhaka and its industrial suburbs, forcing 529 factories to halt production, according to figures from the manufacturers' association BGMEA reported by The Business Standard.

The meeting came at the end of a day in which workers set a police vehicle on fire beneath a metro station in Dhaka's Mirpur district, three metro stations were shut for about two hours, and police detained around 20 people. Factory owners warned that they could close factories temporarily under the country's labour law if workers did not go back to work, even though the government had formed a new minimum wage board that morning.

## What happened

Workers blocked the Mirpur-10 roundabout from about 9.30 am local time (9 am IST) on Sunday. Police gave them until 11 am to clear the road and moved in at about 11.15 am, The Business Standard (TBS) reported. Protesters threw bricks and stones; police used batons, tear gas, sound grenades and water cannon, according to TBS and bdnews24.

Protesters set fire to a police vehicle under the Mirpur-11 metro station at about 12.30 pm, Prothom Alo reported. The Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11 and Pallabi stations on Dhaka's metro line were closed from noon, an inspector of the metro rail police, Mohammad Mohsin Sheikh, said, citing security reasons. TBS put the closure at noon to 2 pm and Prothom Alo at noon to 2.30 pm. The area was calm by about 2 pm.

The deputy commissioner of police for Mirpur, Hassan Mohammad Naser Rikabdar, told TBS at 8 pm that 19 people had been detained and legal action was being taken. Prothom Alo, citing police, put the number at 20, nine of them in Gazipur and 11 in Mirpur.

A deputy commissioner of the Detective Branch, Mohammad Rakib Khan, alleged that those detained in Mirpur were activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliates who had come from several districts to "sabotage" the labour movement, TBS reported. A joint commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Mohidul Islam, said police suspected that a group opposed to the government had joined the protests. The Awami League's response to the allegation had not been reported, and no evidence was made public.

North of the capital, workers in Gazipur's Kaliakair blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway from about 8.30 am until about 3 pm, and set fire to three places in the Palli Bidyut area, including a factory warehouse, Prothom Alo reported, citing the local fire service. A police box under the Konabari flyover and a police vehicle were also set alight.

Workers and police officers were injured, according to TBS and Al Jazeera, but no figures were given. No deaths had been reported by Sunday night.

## The prime minister's meeting

Tarique Rahman met Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury and other officials in the Cabinet Division conference room at the Secretariat from about 6 pm, according to bdnews24 and Prothom Alo. The coordinator of the ruling BNP's labour wing also attended, Prothom Alo reported.

The prime minister told everyone concerned to stay alert to keep factories running and protect lives and property, TBS reported. No other decisions had been announced. The home minister is expected to meet factory owners on Monday, according to TBS.

Earlier in the day the labour minister cancelled a planned visit to the UAE. "Vested interests are conspiring to create instability ahead of December and destabilise the government," he told reporters, according to TBS. He did not say who he meant.

## How many factories are shut

The figures vary. TBS, citing BGMEA sources, reported that 529 factories employing more than 10 lakh (1 million) workers halted production on Sunday. Prothom Alo and bdnews24 put the number of factories that declared a holiday in Mirpur, Kaliakair, Savar and Ashulia at about 300. Industrial police had earlier given figures of at least 45 in Gazipur and more than 50 in Ashulia. Owners told TBS that at least 20 factories had been attacked.

## The wage board

The labour ministry formed a six-member minimum wage board for the garment sector on Sunday morning, headed by a senior district and sessions judge, Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman. It includes two owners' representatives (from the BGMEA and the Bangladesh Employers' Federation), two workers' representatives, including the BNP-aligned Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal's president, and a Dhaka University professor as the independent member, according to Prothom Alo and TBS. No deadline for its recommendations has been reported.

Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000. The current minimum is Tk 12,500, Al Jazeera reported. A labour ministry adviser, M Sakhawat Hossain Chowdhury, said the wage board issue "has been resolved" and that workers should return to work. Labour leaders told TBS the government had delayed forming the board for nearly two months.

## What they are saying

The president of the BGMEA, Mahmud Hasan Khan Babu, told TBS that if workers still refused to work or turned to vandalism after the board was formed, "it would indicate that they have other motives". He said owners could then close factories under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, which allows owners to shut a factory temporarily. BGMEA and the knitwear makers' body BKMEA warned that factories could stay closed indefinitely.

Exporters are worried about orders. The managing director of one knitwear firm told TBS that nearly 40% of its annual export orders come between October and February, when buyers place orders for the next season.

## Background

Garments earn more than 80% of Bangladesh's export income, about $38.7 billion in the year to June 2026, and employ about four million people, TBS reported. Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China.

The protests began last week in Mirpur and spread to Gazipur, Ashulia and Savar. The government deployed Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) in Gazipur's industrial areas on Sunday; the force says it will stay until 7 November. Workers point to rising prices and a recent pay rise for government employees; owners say orders have weakened and costs have risen.

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

India's apparel exporters compete with Bangladesh for orders from the same global brands, and buyers worried about delays may look elsewhere in the region. Bangladesh also buys cotton, yarn and fabric from India, much of it by road through West Bengal's Petrapole-Benapole crossing, so a long shutdown would hit traders and transporters on the Indian side.

Stability in Dhaka also matters for India-Bangladesh relations. Officials of the two countries are due to meet in Dhaka on 17 and 18 November, when Bangladesh says it will raise the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.

## What happens next

- Monday: the home minister is expected to meet factory owners, according to TBS.
- The new wage board has not yet announced its first meeting.
- BGB personnel stay in Gazipur's industrial areas until 7 November.

## Key numbers

- 529: factories that halted production on Sunday (BGMEA sources, via TBS)
- 10 lakh+: workers at those factories (TBS)
- Tk 30,000: the minimum monthly wage workers want
- Tk 12,500: the current minimum (Al Jazeera)
- 19-20: people detained on Sunday (police, via TBS and Prothom Alo)
